name: Backhand push
summary: A short, controlled backspin return against backspin, played in front of the body.
whenToUse: Against short or half-long backspin to your backhand when you can't (or don't want to) attack it. It keeps the ball low and safe.

keyPoints.stance: Square to the table. For short balls, step in under the table with your right foot (left foot if left-handed).
keyPoints.bodyAction: Lean in from the hips. The body stays quiet; the push is a small forearm movement.
keyPoints.strokeLength: Short. The bat moves forward and slightly down, finishing pointing at the target.
keyPoints.timing: Early: at the top of the bounce or just before, to keep the return low.
keyPoints.tablePosition: Close to the table, stepping in for short balls.
keyPoints.freeArm: Relaxed, out to the side for balance.
keyPoints.batArm: Bat face open, about halfway between flat and facing up. Contact on the lower back of the ball.
keyPoints.recovery: Step back out to ready after the push. Don't stay leaning over the table.
keyPoints.anticipation: Heavy backspin needs a more open bat and more forward push; light backspin needs a flatter bat.

learningPath.task: Watch the 3D player from the side so you can see the open bat face.
learningPath.passCheck: You can say the three cues.

learningPath.task: Follow-along mode: step in, push, step out.
learningPath.passCheck: 3 sets of 10, then yes to all self-checks.
selfChecks: Was your bat face open at contact?
Did the bat move forward, not just down?
Did you step back out to ready?

learningPath.task: First contact against slow backspin. Just keep the ball on the table.
Push rally until 20 in a row, every ball low over the net.
Push, then drive when the ball comes long.
Receive serves with a push and play the point out.
Test: backhand pushes in a row.
learningPath.passCheck: 20 in a row, all low over the net.

gamePatterns.situation: A short backspin serve to your backhand.
gamePatterns.how: Push it long and fast to their backhand corner, or short and low if they are waiting to attack.
Push deep and to the corners. Wait for a long or high ball, then attack it.

causes: Contact too late, as the ball falls

troubleshooting.symptom: The ball goes into the net
causes: Bat not open enough for the backspin
fixes: Open the face more against heavy backspin
Push through the ball toward the target

causes: Blocking the ball instead of brushing under it
fixes: Brush the lower back of the ball

troubleshooting.symptom: The ball goes off the end
causes: Standing too far back for short balls
fixes: Step in so you play the ball close to the bounce

penholdNotes: Use the same side of the bat with the wrist turned so the face opens; the forearm action is the same.
